seeds.text: Classify Orchestrator/runtime/UI actions by both confirmation level (none | light | strong | hard_gate) and reversibility (immediate_undo | compensating_action_only | non_reversible), replacing ad hoc per-surface confirmation behavior.

Adopt working interpretations: none = safe navigation/focus and low-risk presentation without user-data or live-runtime mutation; light = moderate-impact actions with plausible mis-clicks; strong = discard local state, remove artifacts/worktrees, revoke accepted state, or materially change live execution; hard_gate = canonical approval/blocked/HITL flows that generic UI cannot bypass.

Map action families: none — open/focus/navigate/deep-link, evidence/history/ledger/source control, tab-local filter/sort/search; light — minor acknowledge/dismiss, switch focused run, open resolution thread; strong — pause/cancel run, retry from safe point, prune worktree/clean workspace, prune evidence, revoke promotion, merge/split concerns; hard_gate — HITL approve/reject, graph patch application affecting canonical graph generation, remote-side-effect actions under explicit non-bypassable policy.

Use a shared governance/runtime record envelope: record_id, record_kind, project_id, optional run_id, scope refs (seam_id, package_id, node_id, attempt_id, promotion_id, concern_id, lane_id, worktree_id), status, created_at_utc, created_by_kind, created_by_ref, optional superseded_by_record_id, plus source_refs[], artifact_refs[], evidence_refs[], summary, optional detail_ref.

hard_gate confirmations must surface runtime-defined allowed actions, why the gate exists, exact consequence of each allowed action, and no hidden alternative path; strong confirmations must include reversibility class and whether local work/artifacts/history remain.
Do not label actions as Undo when the system only supports compensating paths; prefer labels such as Reopen, Restore, Retry from Safe Point, Create New Lane, Re-request Promotion, Reapply.
Delete Run in History remains questionable until delete semantics, authorization, and reversibility are defined relative to lineage and ledger records.
